q: What are the substances that take part in a chemical reaction called? [JAC 2022]
e: Initial substances taking part in a reaction are reactants; newly formed substances are products, rate modifiers are catalysts, and insoluble solids are precipitates.

q: What are the new substances formed during a chemical reaction called?
e: New substances formed as a result of a reaction and written on the right side of the arrow are called products, while substances on the left are reactants.

q: On the basis of which law is a chemical equation balanced? [JAC 2022, 2024]
e: According to the law of conservation of mass, mass is neither created nor destroyed, so the number of atoms of each element must be equal on both sides.

q: In a chemical reaction, the total mass of products compared to the total mass of reactants is: [JAC 2022]
e: By the law of conservation of mass, the total mass of products is always equal to the total mass of reactants.

q: Which of the following observations helps determine that a chemical reaction has taken place? [JAC 2022]
o: Evolution of gas and temperature change
e: Change in state, colour, temperature, and evolution of a gas are all standard experimental indicators of a chemical reaction.

q: Why is magnesium ribbon rubbed with sandpaper before burning it in air?
o: To remove the protective magnesium oxide layer
e: Magnesium develops a surface layer of magnesium oxide/carbonate on exposure to air that hinders burning, so sandpaper removes it.

q: Magnesium ribbon burns in air with a flame of which appearance?
e: Magnesium reacts vigorously with oxygen, burning with a dazzling white flame to form a white powder of magnesium oxide (MgO).

q: What is the chemical formula of quick lime?
e: Calcium oxide (CaO) is quick lime, whereas Ca(OH)2 is slaked lime and CaCO3 is marble/limestone.

q: The solution of which substance is used for whitewashing walls (formed when quick lime reacts with water)? [JAC 2022]
e: As per NCERT, substance X is calcium oxide (CaO), which reacts with water to form calcium hydroxide [Ca(OH)2] used for whitewashing.

q: What is the chemical formula of marble?
e: Marble has the chemical formula CaCO3 (calcium carbonate); it is also formed on walls when Ca(OH)2 reacts slowly with atmospheric CO2.

q: What type of chemical reaction is 2H2(g) + O2(g) → 2H2O(l)? [JAC 2022]
e: When two or more reactants combine to form a single product (here water), it is a combination reaction.

q: Reactions in which heat is released along with the formation of products are called:
e: Exothermic reactions evolve heat with product formation, whereas endothermic reactions absorb heat.

q: Which of the following processes is an exothermic reaction? [JAC 2022, 2026]
e: During respiration, glucose combines with oxygen to form CO2, H2O, and releases energy, making it an exothermic process.

q: The decomposition of vegetable matter into compost is an example of which reaction?
e: Decomposition of vegetable matter into compost releases heat energy, making it an exothermic reaction.

q: What type of reaction is CH4 + 2O2 → CO2 + 2H2O + energy? [JAC 2022]
e: Combustion of methane (natural gas) releases heat energy, hence it is an exothermic reaction.

q: Which of the following reactions is an endothermic reaction? [JAC 2025]
o: Decomposition of calcium carbonate into quick lime and CO2
e: Thermal decomposition of calcium carbonate absorbs heat energy, so it is endothermic; the other three release energy.

q: A reaction in which a single reactant breaks down to give simpler products is called:
e: When a single reactant breaks down into simpler products using heat, light, or electricity, it is called a decomposition reaction.

q: Which type of reaction is 2NaHCO3 → Na2CO3 + H2O + CO2? [JAC 2022]
e: Here a single compound (NaHCO3) breaks down into three simpler substances, so it is a decomposition reaction.

q: Which of the following is an example of photolytic decomposition? [JAC 2022]
e: Silver bromide (2AgBr → 2Ag + Br2) decomposes in sunlight (photolysis); water undergoes electrolysis and CaCO3 undergoes thermal decomposition.

q: Which compound is used in black and white photography? [JAC 2024]
e: AgCl and AgBr decompose in sunlight to give silver metal, making them essential in black and white photography.

q: What type of reaction is Fe(s) + CuSO4(aq) → FeSO4(aq) + Cu(s)? [JAC 2024]
e: More reactive iron displaces less reactive copper from copper sulphate solution, so it is a displacement reaction.

q: The given reaction Fe2O3 + 2Al → Al2O3 + 2Fe is an example of a: [JAC 2021]
e: Aluminium displaces iron from iron(III) oxide, so this is a displacement reaction.

q: What is the reaction AB + CD → AD + CB called? [JAC 2020, 2022]
e: A reaction in which there is an exchange of ions between the reactants is called a double displacement reaction.

q: During oxidation of a substance in a reaction, what occurs? [JAC 2022]
o: Gain of oxygen or loss of hydrogen
e: Oxidation involves gain of oxygen or loss of hydrogen; reduction involves loss of oxygen or gain of hydrogen.

q: When a metal is attacked by substances around it such as moisture and acids, the process is called:
e: The slow deterioration of metals by moisture, air, or acids is known as corrosion (e.g., rusting of iron).

q: The change in smell and taste of fat and oil containing foods when kept for a long time is called:
e: Oxidation of fats and oils causing bad smell and taste is called rancidity.

q: Which gas is flushed into bags of chips to prevent them from becoming rancid? [JAC 2022, 2026]
e: Nitrogen is relatively unreactive and displaces oxygen, preventing oxidation (rancidity) of oils in chips.

q: Rancidity is caused by which chemical process? [JAC 2022]
e: Rancidity occurs due to the aerial oxidation of fats and oils present in food.

q: Which of the following is NOT a physical change? [JAC 2026]
e: Caramelization involves thermal chemical breakdown of sugar into new compounds, making it a chemical change rather than a physical change.

q: Which symbol represents an aqueous solution in a balanced chemical equation?
e: In chemical equations, (s) stands for solid, (l) for liquid, (g) for gas, and (aq) for aqueous solution in water.

q: When an iron nail is dipped in blue copper sulphate solution, the solution turns: [JAC 2022, 2026]
e: Iron displaces copper to form pale green ferrous sulphate (FeSO4), while reddish-brown copper deposits on the nail.

q: When green ferrous sulphate crystals (FeSO4·7H2O) are heated gently, their colour first changes to:
e: On gentle heating, FeSO4·7H2O loses water of crystallisation to form white anhydrous FeSO4 before decomposing into brown Fe2O3.

q: On strong heating of ferrous sulphate crystals, the characteristic smell of burning sulphur is due to:
e: Ferrous sulphate decomposes as 2FeSO4 → Fe2O3 + SO2 + SO3; the evolved SO2 and SO3 gases produce the smell of burning sulphur.

q: Which brown-coloured gas is evolved when lead nitrate [Pb(NO3)2] powder is heated in a boiling tube?
e: Thermal decomposition of lead nitrate yields yellow PbO, oxygen, and brown fumes of nitrogen dioxide (NO2).

q: The mole (and volume) ratio of hydrogen and oxygen gases liberated during electrolysis of water is: [JAC 2025]
e: Since 2H2O → 2H2 + O2, two volumes of hydrogen at the cathode are collected for every one volume of oxygen at the anode (2:1).

q: Why are a few drops of dilute sulphuric acid added to water during its electrolysis?
o: To increase the electrical conductivity of water
e: Pure water is a poor conductor of electricity; adding dilute H2SO4 provides ions to increase its electrical conductivity.

q: White silver chloride (AgCl) kept in sunlight turns into which colour?
e: Sunlight decomposes white AgCl into grey silver metal and chlorine gas: 2AgCl → 2Ag + Cl2.

q: When sodium sulphate and barium chloride solutions are mixed, what precipitate is formed?
e: Ba²⁺ ions react with SO4²⁻ ions to form an insoluble white precipitate of barium sulphate (BaSO4).

q: Mixing lead nitrate and potassium iodide solutions forms a precipitate of which colour and compound?
e: Pb(NO3)2 reacts with KI in a double displacement reaction to form a bright yellow precipitate of lead iodide (PbI2).

q: When hydrogen sulphide gas is passed through blue copper sulphate solution, the colour of the precipitate is: [JAC 2026]
e: Hydrogen sulphide reacts with copper sulphate in a double displacement reaction to give a black precipitate of copper sulphide (CuS).

q: When copper powder is heated in a china dish, the black surface coating formed is:
e: Copper reacts with oxygen upon heating to form a black coating of copper(II) oxide (CuO).

q: When hydrogen gas is passed over heated black copper(II) oxide, the black coating turns:
e: Hydrogen reduces black CuO back to brown copper metal while forming steam: CuO + H2 → Cu + H2O.

q: In the reaction ZnO + C → Zn + CO, which substance is getting oxidised? [JAC 2022]
e: Carbon (C) gains oxygen to form CO, so C is oxidised, while ZnO loses oxygen and is reduced.

q: In the reaction CuO + H2 → Cu + H2O, which substances are oxidised and reduced respectively? [JAC 2022]
e: H2 gains oxygen so H2 is oxidised, whereas CuO loses oxygen so CuO is reduced.

q: In the reaction MnO2 + 4HCl → MnCl2 + 2H2O + Cl2, which substance is reduced?
e: MnO2 loses oxygen to form MnCl2, so MnO2 is reduced, while HCl loses hydrogen to be oxidised into Cl2.

q: Which among the following is a double displacement reaction? [JAC 2025]
e: Na2SO4 + BaCl2 involves mutual exchange of ions between both ionic compounds; Pb + CuCl2 is single displacement.

q: Adding water to quick lime during whitewashing evolves heat; what type of reaction is this? [JAC 2022]
e: CaO combines with H2O to form a single product Ca(OH)2 with release of heat, so it is an exothermic combination reaction.

q: What happens when dilute hydrochloric acid is added to iron filings? [JAC 2022 NCERT]
o: Hydrogen gas and iron chloride are produced
Chlorine gas and iron hydroxide are produced
Iron salt and water are produced
e: Iron reacts with dilute HCl in a displacement reaction: Fe + 2HCl → FeCl2 + H2, forming iron(II) chloride and hydrogen gas.

q: What type of reaction is Pb + CuCl2 → PbCl2 + Cu? [JAC 2022]
e: Lead is more reactive than copper and displaces copper from CuCl2, making it a displacement reaction.

q: After whitewashing, the shiny finish appears on walls after 2–3 days due to formation of:
e: Slaked lime Ca(OH)2 slowly reacts with atmospheric CO2 to form a shiny thin layer of calcium carbonate (CaCO3).

q: What is the chemical composition/formula of rust formed on iron?
e: Rust is hydrated iron(III) oxide with the general formula Fe2O3·xH2O.

q: Silver articles turn black after some time when exposed to air due to formation of a coating of:
e: Silver reacts with hydrogen sulphide in air to form a black tarnish coating of silver sulphide (Ag2S).

q: When a copper vessel is exposed to moist air for a long time, it acquires a coating of which colour?
e: Copper reacts with moist CO2 in air to lose its shine and form a green coating of basic copper carbonate.

q: Heating limestone gives CaCO3(s) → CaO(s) + CO2(g); this reaction is an example of:
e: Decomposition carried out by heating is called thermal decomposition; quick lime produced here is widely used in cement manufacture.

q: A reaction in which both oxidation and reduction take place simultaneously is called:
e: Reactions involving simultaneous oxidation of one reactant and reduction of another are called oxidation-reduction or redox reactions.

q: What type of product is characteristically formed in a precipitation reaction?
e: Any reaction that produces a water-insoluble solid (precipitate) is called a precipitation reaction.

q: Substances added to foods containing fats and oils to prevent rancidity are called:
e: Antioxidants inhibit aerial oxidation and therefore prevent rancidity in fatty and oily foods.

q: When a strip of zinc is placed in copper sulphate solution, zinc sulphate and copper form because:
o: Copper is more reactive than zinc
Zinc is more reactive than copper
e: Zinc lies above copper in the reactivity series, so more reactive Zn displaces Cu from CuSO4 to form colourless ZnSO4.

q: If a gas evolved in a reaction burns with a "pop" sound near a burning splinter, the gas is: [JAC 2022]
e: Hydrogen gas is combustible and burns with a characteristic "pop" sound when tested with a burning flame.

q: Which reaction occurs and which gas is evolved when dilute sulphuric acid is added to zinc granules?
e: Zn displaces hydrogen from dilute H2SO4 liberating H2 gas and heat, warming the conical flask.

q: Which of the following chemical equations is correctly balanced? [JAC 2022]
e: In 3Fe + 4H2O → Fe3O4 + 4H2, both sides have 3 Fe atoms, 8 H atoms, and 4 O atoms.

q: Find the balancing coefficients x, y, and z in: x Pb(NO3)2(s) → y PbO(s) + z NO2(g) + O2(g)
e: The balanced equation is 2Pb(NO3)2 → 2PbO + 4NO2 + O2, so x=2, y=2, z=4.

q: In the balanced equation a FeSO4 → Fe2O3 + b SO2 + c SO3, the values of a, b, and c are:
e: Balanced equation is 2FeSO4 → Fe2O3 + SO2 + SO3 (2 Fe, 2 S, 8 O on each side), giving a=2, b=1, c=1.

q: Which of the following chemical equations is balanced? [JAC 2022]
e: Zn + CuSO4 → ZnSO4 + Cu has equal numbers of Zn, Cu, S, and O atoms on both sides; the others are unbalanced.

q: Upon balancing p Al + q O2 → r Al2O3 with smallest whole numbers, p, q, and r are:
e: The balanced equation is 4Al + 3O2 → 2Al2O3, giving 4 Al and 6 O atoms on each side.

q: In the balanced equation for photosynthesis 6CO2 + 12H2O → C6H12O6 + 6O2 + x H2O, what is x?
e: Reactants have 24 H and 24 O atoms; since C6H12O6 uses 12 H and 6 O and 6O2 uses 12 O, x must be 6 H2O.

q: For the balanced reaction N2 + a H2 → b NH3, the coefficients a and b are:
e: Balanced equation: N2 + 3H2 → 2NH3, so a=3 and b=2.

q: In C6H12O6 + x O2 → y CO2 + z H2O, what is the sum x + y + z when balanced?
e: Balanced equation is C6H12O6 + 6O2 → 6CO2 + 6H2O, so x + y + z = 6 + 6 + 6 = 18.

q: In the reaction 2H2S + SO2 → 2H2O + 3S, identify the oxidised and reduced substances respectively:
e: H2S loses hydrogen to form S (oxidised), while SO2 loses oxygen to form S (reduced).

q: A shiny brown-coloured element X on heating in air becomes black in colour. Identify X and the black compound:
e: Brown copper (Cu) oxidises on heating in air to form black copper(II) oxide (CuO).

q: Which equation correctly represents the balanced reaction between AgNO3 and NaCl, or HCl and NaOH? [JAC 2022]
e: AgNO3 + NaCl → NaNO3 + AgCl is already balanced (1 Ag, 1 N, 3 O, 1 Na, 1 Cl on each side); the other three are unbalanced.

q: Where is the exothermic displacement reaction Fe2O3(s) + 2Al(s) → Al2O3(s) + 2Fe(l) + heat practically used?
o: Joining railway tracks or cracked machine parts (thermit welding)
e: The intense heat produced melts the iron formed, which is used in thermit welding to join railway tracks and cracked machine parts.

q: In CO(g) + 2H2(g) → CH3OH(l), why is "340 atm" written above the reaction arrow?
e: Reaction conditions such as temperature, pressure (340 atm), and catalyst are written above or below the arrow.

q: If 20 g of CaCO3 is completely decomposed in a closed container, what will be the total mass of CaO and CO2 formed?
e: By the law of conservation of mass in a closed vessel, total product mass equals the reactant mass (20 g).

q: How many grams of CO2 are formed when 12 g of carbon burns completely in 32 g of oxygen?
e: Since C + O2 → CO2 and mass is conserved, 12 g + 32 g = 44 g of CO2 is produced.

q: Magnesium burns in nitrogen atmosphere to form magnesium nitride; the balanced equation is:
e: Magnesium nitride has formula Mg3N2 (Mg²⁺ and N³⁻), so the balanced reaction is 3Mg + N2 → Mg3N2.

q: In 2Mg + O2 → 2MgO, if 24 g of Mg reacts completely with 16 g of O2, how much MgO is formed?
e: 24 g Mg and 16 g O2 react completely in stoichiometric ratio to produce 40 g of MgO.

q: Mixing barium hydroxide and ammonium chloride makes the test tube feel cold to touch; what type of reaction is it?
e: Since the test tube cools down, heat is absorbed from the surroundings, proving it is an endothermic reaction.

q: Which reaction is simultaneously a combination reaction and an exothermic reaction?
e: Quick lime combines with water to form a single product Ca(OH)2 while releasing substantial heat.

q: In the reaction H2S + Cl2 → 2HCl + S, identify the reducing agent:
e: H2S supplies hydrogen to reduce Cl2 to HCl while itself getting oxidised to S, so H2S is the reducing agent.

q: Select the balanced equation for the reaction between sodium hydroxide and sulphuric acid:
e: In 2NaOH + H2SO4 → Na2SO4 + 2H2O, both sides have 2 Na, 1 S, 4 H, and 6 O atoms.

q: What happens when a silver strip is dipped in copper sulphate solution?
e: Silver is less reactive than copper, so it cannot displace copper from CuSO4 solution.

q: Identify the balanced equation for the reaction of potassium bromide with barium iodide:
e: 2KBr + BaI2 → 2KI + BaBr2 balances all K, Br, Ba, and I atoms properly.

q: Why is silver bromide stored in dark-coloured (amber/black) bottles?
o: To block sunlight and prevent photolytic decomposition
e: Dark bottles cut off light and prevent photolytic decomposition of AgBr into Ag and Br2.

q: What are the products formed when zinc metal reacts with silver nitrate (AgNO3) solution?
e: More reactive zinc displaces silver from AgNO3 to form zinc nitrate Zn(NO3)2 and silver.

q: Hydrogen reacts with chlorine in sunlight to form hydrogen chloride; the balanced equation is:
e: Both hydrogen and chlorine exist as diatomic molecules, so the balanced combination equation is H2 + Cl2 → 2HCl.

q: In complete combustion of butane C4H10 + x O2 → 4CO2 + 5H2O, what is the value of coefficient x?
e: Products contain 8 + 5 = 13 oxygen atoms, so x = 13/2 = 6.5 (or 2, 13, 8, 10 in smallest integer form).

q: How does keeping oily food in airtight containers help prevent rancidity?
o: Limited air/oxygen supply slows down oxidation
e: Airtight containers restrict contact with atmospheric oxygen, drastically slowing down the oxidation of fats and oils.

q: In 4Na + O2 → 2Na2O, identify the substance oxidised and the substance reduced respectively:
e: Sodium gains oxygen/loses electrons (oxidised), while oxygen gains electrons to form oxide ions (reduced).

q: If zinc granules are added to green ferrous sulphate (FeSO4) solution, what change is observed?
o: Green colour slowly fades and greyish-black iron deposits
e: Zinc is more reactive than iron, so it displaces Fe from FeSO4, forming colourless ZnSO4 and depositing iron metal.

Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
e: Both A and R are true, and the 2:1 atomic ratio in H2O accounts for collecting double the volume of H2 at the cathode.

q:
Assertion (A): Copper powder forms a black coating of CuO upon heating in air.
Reason (R): This is an example of reduction of copper.
o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
e: A is true, but R is false because copper gains oxygen, so it undergoes oxidation rather than reduction.

q:
Assertion (A): Whitewashed walls appear shiny after 2–3 days.
Reason (R): Slaked lime reacts with atmospheric oxygen to form CaO.
o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
e: A is true, but R is false because Ca(OH)2 reacts with atmospheric CO2 to form shiny CaCO3, not with O2 to form CaO.

q:
Assertion (A): Whenever one substance is oxidised in a reaction, another is necessarily reduced.
Reason (R): Oxidation and reduction are complementary processes involving transfer between reactants.
o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
e: Both A and R are true, and R explains why oxidation and reduction always occur together as redox processes.

q: A student places a copper wire in AgNO3 solution (tube P) and an iron nail in CuSO4 solution (tube Q). In which test tube(s) will a reaction occur?
e: Copper is more reactive than silver (reaction occurs in P forming blue Cu(NO3)2) and iron is more reactive than copper (reaction occurs in Q forming green FeSO4).

q: A white solid "X" on heating gives a yellow residue "Y", brown fumes "Z", and oxygen gas. Identify X, Y, Z:
e: Lead nitrate [Pb(NO3)2] thermally decomposes into yellow lead oxide (PbO), brown NO2 gas, and O2 gas.

q: Mixing two clear colourless solutions BaCl2(aq) and Na2SO4(aq) immediately forms a white insoluble solid settling down. This reaction is classified as:
e: Mutual ion exchange makes it a double displacement reaction, and formation of insoluble white BaSO4 makes it a precipitation reaction.

q: A food inspector noticed snacks without nitrogen turned smelly in 10 days while nitrogen-flushed packets stayed fresh. What is the chemical reason?
o: Fats get oxidised in presence of oxygen causing rancidity
e: Oils and fats undergo aerial oxidation to form foul-smelling compounds; nitrogen prevents oxidation by displacing oxygen.

q: A mason added quick lime to a bucket of water and noticed the bucket became very hot. Select the correct chemical description:
e: Calcium oxide reacts vigorously with water to produce slaked lime Ca(OH)2, releasing large amounts of heat (exothermic combination).

q: Heating zinc oxide with carbon at high temperature to extract zinc represents:
e: In ZnO + C → Zn + CO, ZnO is reduced to Zn and carbon is oxidised to CO; hence it is a redox reaction.

q: A student puts a magnesium ribbon in beaker A containing CuSO4(aq) and a silver coin in beaker B containing CuSO4(aq). What is seen after 30 minutes?
o: Blue colour disappears in A with brown Cu deposit; no change in B
e: Mg displaces Cu forming colourless MgSO4, whereas silver is below copper in reactivity and causes no reaction in B.

q: Which statement accurately describes the reaction 2KClO3(s) → 2KCl(s) + 3O2(g)?
o: It is a decomposition reaction liberating oxygen gas
It is a double displacement reaction
e: A single reactant potassium chlorate breaks down to form KCl and O2 gas, making it a decomposition reaction.

q: In electrolysis of water, a student observes that one test tube collects half the gas volume of the other. Identify that gas and electrode:
e: Oxygen (1 volume, half of H2's 2 volumes) is liberated at the positively charged anode.

q: Souring of milk, rusting of iron, and simple melting of candle wax—how many of these are chemical changes?
e: Souring of milk and rusting of iron are chemical changes, while melting of wax is merely a physical change of state.

q: Consider the reaction: 3MnO2(s) + 4Al(s) → 3Mn(l) + 2Al2O3(s) + heat. Which statement is INCORRECT?
o: MnO2 acts as an oxidising agent
It is an exothermic displacement reaction
Al2O3 is being reduced to Mn
e: Al is oxidised to Al2O3 and MnO2 is reduced to Mn (acting as oxidising agent); saying Al2O3 is reduced to Mn is false.

q: In the blast furnace reaction Fe2O3 + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO2, identify the reducing agent and oxidising agent respectively:
e: CO gains oxygen to become CO2 (reducing agent), while Fe2O3 supplies oxygen and gets reduced to Fe (oxidising agent).

q: A white solid A on heating gives residue B and gas C. Adding water to B forms D. Passing gas C into clear solution D regenerates milkiness A. Identify A, B, C, D:
e: CaCO3 decomposes to CaO + CO2; CaO dissolves in water to form Ca(OH)2 (lime water), which turns milky again with CO2 forming CaCO3.

q: Why does the milkiness of lime water disappear when excess CO2 is bubbled through it?
o: Soluble calcium hydrogen carbonate [Ca(HCO3)2] is formed
e: Excess CO2 reacts with insoluble CaCO3 and water to form water-soluble calcium bicarbonate Ca(HCO3)2, clearing the milkiness.

q: When balanced in smallest whole-number integers, which equation has the highest sum of all stoichiometric coefficients (reactants + products)?
e: Balanced 4NH3 + 5O2 → 4NO + 6H2O has coefficient sum 4+5+4+6 = 19, exceeding 3Fe+4H2O→Fe3O4+4H2 (sum=12), N2+3H2→2NH3 (sum=6), and 2H2+O2→2H2O (sum=5).

q: A blue crystalline salt turns white on heating and regains its blue colour when a few drops of water are added. What is the salt?
e: Hydrated copper sulphate (CuSO4·5H2O) loses its 5 water molecules to become white anhydrous CuSO4, which turns blue again upon rehydration.

q: Which statement about double displacement reactions like AgNO3 + NaCl → AgCl + NaNO3 is scientifically TRUE?
o: Oxidation states of ions do not change, so they are non-redox reactions
e: Because the oxidation states/charges of all ions remain unchanged during ion exchange, precipitation/double displacement reactions are non-redox.

q: For the reaction H2S + I2 → 2HI + S, select the completely correct statement:
o: I2 is oxidised and H2S is oxidising agent
I2 is reduced to HI and acts as an oxidising agent
e: I2 gains hydrogen to form HI (so I2 is reduced) while oxidising H2S to S, making I2 the oxidising agent.

q: A metal "M" corrodes slowly in moist air to form a green layer, but on strong heating in air directly forms a black oxide. Identify M:
e: Copper develops a green basic carbonate patina in moist air, whereas strong heating in air forms black CuO.

q: What happens when aqueous solutions of NaCl and KNO3 are mixed together?
o: No precipitate forms as all possible ions/salts remain soluble
e: Since NaCl, KNO3, KCl, and NaNO3 are all completely soluble in water, the ions stay dissociated with no precipitation reaction.

q: In the reaction Cl2 + 2NaOH → NaCl + NaClO + H2O, which element undergoes both oxidation and reduction simultaneously?
e: Chlorine (oxidation state 0) is simultaneously reduced to NaCl (-1) and oxidised to NaClO (+1), a disproportionation reaction.

q: In galvanisation, why does the coating continue to protect iron from rusting even if the coating gets scratched?
o: Copper layer as copper is inert
Zinc layer, because zinc is more reactive than iron and oxidises preferentially
e: Galvanisation coats iron with zinc; since zinc is more reactive than iron, zinc gets oxidised preferentially even when scratched.

q: When copper turnings react with concentrated nitric acid (HNO3), which brown gas is evolved?
e: Concentrated HNO3 is a strong oxidising agent that oxidises copper to Cu(NO3)2 while liberating reddish-brown NO2 gas.

q: Comparing 2H2(g) + O2(g) → 2H2O(l) with 2H2(g) + O2(g) → 2H2O(g), which reaction releases more heat?
o: The one forming liquid H2O releases more heat
e: Condensing steam to liquid water releases additional latent heat of vaporisation, so forming H2O(l) releases more total heat.

q: Which combination of processes occurs when a wax candle burns?
o: Both physical (melting of wax) and chemical (combustion of wax vapour) changes
e: Melting of wax near the wick is a physical change, whereas burning of wax vapours into CO2 and H2O is a chemical change.

q: During rusting of iron (4Fe + 3O2 + 2x H2O → 2Fe2O3·xH2O), iron metal is oxidised to which oxidation state?
e: In Fe2O3 (ferric oxide), three O²⁻ ions balance two Fe³⁺ ions, so iron is oxidised from 0 to +3.

q: A student performs three thermal decomposition experiments: FeSO4, Pb(NO3)2, and CaCO3. How many yield a pungent or coloured gas?
e: FeSO4 gives pungent SO2/SO3 and Pb(NO3)2 gives brown NO2, whereas CaCO3 releases colourless, odourless CO2.

q: Which of the following decomposition reactions produces three distinct product compounds from a single reactant?
e: 2FeSO4 thermally decomposes into three different products: solid Fe2O3, SO2 gas, and SO3 gas; the others give only two products.

q: When aqueous potassium iodide (KI) is mixed with aqueous silver nitrate (AgNO3), what is formed?
o: Yellow precipitate of AgI and KNO3 solution
e: Silver iodide (AgI) precipitates as a yellow solid while KNO3 stays dissolved.

q: At the end of heating solid copper(II) nitrate [2Cu(NO3)2 → 2CuO + 4NO2 + O2], what is the colour of the solid residue left?
e: The solid residue left is copper(II) oxide (CuO), which is black in colour (unlike yellow PbO).

q: Under which condition will an iron nail rust the fastest?
o: Boiled distilled water covered with an oil layer
Open vessel with salt water and air
e: Rusting requires both oxygen and water, and dissolved salts act as electrolytes that sharply accelerate the corrosion process.

q: In the reaction H2O2 + Cl2 → 2HCl + O2, hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) acts as:
e: H2O2 supplies hydrogen to reduce Cl2 into HCl while itself getting oxidised to O2, so it behaves as a reducing agent.

q: In the combustion of ethene C2H4 + x O2 → y CO2 + z H2O, the balanced coefficients x, y, z are:
e: C2H4 + 3O2 → 2CO2 + 2H2O balances 2 C, 4 H, and 6 O atoms on both sides.

q: Why do gold (Au) and platinum (Pt) resist corrosion in moist air and ordinary acids?
o: Being at the bottom of the reactivity series, they are extremely unreactive (noble metals)
e: Gold and platinum lie at the very bottom of the reactivity series and therefore do not react easily with air, moisture, or dilute acids.

q: In a Class 10 laboratory quiz on colour-change reactions, identify the pair that correctly matches BOTH reaction and precipitate colour:
e: PbI2 is yellow and BaSO4 is white; only CuSO4 + H2S giving a black precipitate of CuS is accurately matched.

q: Why are decomposition reactions called the exact opposite of combination reactions?
o: Combination joins 2+ reactants into 1 product (usually exothermic), whereas decomposition splits 1 reactant into 2+ products using energy
e: Combination merges multiple substances into one (often releasing energy), whereas decomposition uses energy to split a single compound into simpler substances.

q: A metal M forms sulphate MSO4, decolourises blue CuSO4 by depositing copper, yet causes NO change in green FeSO4 solution. What could M be?
o: Pb or Sn (less reactive than Fe, more than Cu)
e: Since M displaces Cu but cannot displace Fe, its reactivity must lie between Fe and Cu (such as Sn or Pb, which form divalent M²⁺ ions).

q: In the redox reaction 2FeCl3 + H2S → 2FeCl2 + 2HCl + S, identify what is oxidised and what is reduced:
o: H2S oxidised to S, FeCl3 reduced to FeCl2
e: H2S loses hydrogen to form S (oxidation), while FeCl3 loses electronegative Cl (Fe³⁺ → Fe²⁺) to form FeCl2 (reduction).

q: What would happen if oxygen gas is filled instead of nitrogen in a packet of potato chips?
o: Chips will stay extra crisp and fresh
Oils will rapidly oxidise causing rancidity and spoiling the chips
e: Oxygen actively oxidises fats and oils in the chips, accelerating rancidity and ruining their taste and odour.

q: Which set of compounds from Class 10 Chapter 1 undergo thermal decomposition, photolytic decomposition, and reduction by H2 respectively?
e: In NCERT Chapter 1, FeSO4 exemplifies thermal decomposition, AgBr photolytic decomposition, and CuO reduction by hydrogen gas.
